7	#   -> a second run is killed mid-turn and resumed to completion.
8	# On success the probed binary versions land in

11	# Usage: release/preflight-real.sh [route ...]

13	
14	set -eu
15	
16	if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then
17	  echo "preflight-real.sh proves real providers and spends real money;" >&2

19	  exit 1
20	fi
21	
22	repo_root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
23	deadreckon_bin=${DEADRECKON_BIN:-"$repo_root/target/release/deadreckon"}
24	known_good="$repo_root/release/known-good-providers.json"

26	operator=${USER:-unknown}
27	
28	if [ ! -x "$deadreckon_bin" ]; then
29	  echo "no release binary at $deadreckon_bin — run 'make build' first," >&2
30	  echo "or point DEADRECKON_BIN at one." >&2
31	  exit 1
32	fi
33	
34	routes=${*:-"cli:claude-code cli:codex"}
35	
36	workdir=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/deadreckon-preflight.XXXXXX")
37	trap 'rm -rf "$workdir"' EXIT INT TERM
38	
39	binary_for_route() {
40	  case "$1" in
41	    cli:claude-code) echo "claude" ;;
42	    cli:codex) echo "codex" ;;
43	    cli:gemini) echo "gemini" ;;
44	    cli:copilot) echo "copilot" ;;
45	    *) echo "" ;;
46	  esac
47	}
48	
49	fresh_repo() {
50	  dir="$workdir/$1-repo"
51	  rm -rf "$dir"
52	  mkdir -p "$dir"
53	  (
54	    cd "$dir"
55	    git init -q
56	    git config user.email preflight@deadreckon.local
57	    git config user.name "deadreckon preflight"

59	    git add README.md

63	}
64	
65	latest_run_id() {
66	  # state.json lives at <home>/runstate/<task>/runs/<run_id>/state.json
67	  find "$1/runstate" -name state.json 2>/dev/null \
68	    | while IFS= read -r state; do
69	        dir=$(dirname "$state")
70	        printf '%s %s\n' "$(stat -f %m "$state" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$state")" "$(basename "$dir")"
71	      done \
72	    | sort -rn | head -n1 | cut -d' ' -f2
73	}
74	
75	results=""
76	
77	for route in $routes; do
78	  echo "==> proving $route"

138	  if [ -n "$results" ]; then

143	  fi
144	done

Analysis:

**`release/preflight-real.sh` changes:**
1. `def-done "README.md gains a comment header naming the file's purpose"` — the argument is a hardcoded string literal in the script, passed as a single argv to the binary. No injection vector.
2. `git add -A && git commit -qm "done criteria"` — runs inside a freshly-created throwaway repo (`fresh_repo`) in a `mktemp -d` workdir. Hardcoded commit message; no attacker-influenced paths.
3. `apply ... --plain --no-confirm` — flag passed to the `deadreckon apply` subcommand. The repo is the throwaway preflight fixture; the only "changes" applied are whatever the agent produced during the same operator-initiated run on a goal the operator chose. There's no privilege boundary crossed here — the operator is already running the same binary in `--mode run --yes` immediately above.

The script is also explicitly gated against CI execution (`if [ -n "${CI:-}" ]; then ... exit 1`), so it only runs when an operator invokes it locally and intentionally spends money. There is no untrusted entry point and no new sink reached by attacker-influenced data.

**`release/known-good-providers.json`:** Pure recorded data — version strings, UUIDs, route identifiers, operator handle. No secrets, no executable content; it is consumed (if at all) as a JSON manifest.

I checked for: shell injection in the new `def-done` arg (literal string, safe); JSON injection via `binary_version` interpolation in the `printf` template (unchanged code, not in the diff); allowlist/gate parity (the new `--no-confirm` is symmetrically applied to the apply step only, which the operator already authorized); fail-open state drift (none — the script `set -eu` and explicitly checks for the signed marker before applying).

No security findings in the diff.
